tentative

/TEN-tuh-tiv/ - the stress falls on TEN · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Tentative means not final or definite; subject to change.

Rehearsals follow a tentative schedule until the theater confirms which nights the main stage is free.

Example

Base camp posted a tentative summit date of May 12. Every climber understood the adjective: the date was real - porters hired, oxygen staged - and the mountain would still overrule it the moment the jet stream shifted.

Tentative is exact because an actual arrangement exists and everyone knows it may move: not a wish, not a guess, a penciled plan. Made-up dates are not tentative, and neither are locked ones. The word lives in that middle state - real, useful, and openly subject to change.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

unconfirmed: Unconfirmed hangs on someone else's answer: a booking, a report, or a rumor stays unconfirmed while you wait for another party to say a final yes. Tentative describes the plan's own status — a real arrangement exists, but its makers have deliberately left it open to change.

changeable: Changeable describes a standing disposition to shift — weather, moods, prices that move for any reason at all, over and over. Tentative marks a one-time status instead: this particular plan is real but not yet final, and it stops being tentative the moment it locks.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

final: closed to further revision

settled: agreed on and no longer in motion

Where it sits · how firmly the plan is fixed

floated → tentative → official

floated vs. tentative: A floated idea is merely tossed into the room to see faces; tentative goes further - an actual arrangement exists, just one that can still move.

official vs. tentative: Official outranks tentative: a tentative date can slide quietly, but an official one is announced, binding, and printed on the tickets.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — tent: to try, test

Suffix — -ative: inclined to

Put it together: Tent (to try, test) + -ative (inclined to) = inclined toward trying. Latin temptare meant 'to test or feel out': a tentative date is one still being tried on for size - pinned up, tested against the weather, and movable until the final fitting.

Use the root in a new word: attempt: Her first attempt at the high bar missed; her second stuck the landing.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral

Tentative is for arrangements - dates, lineups, agreements - that exist but can still move. Unverified, its cluster-mate here, is for claims awaiting a check. You will also meet provisional in this unit's reference list: tentative's dressed-up twin, fond of official paperwork. A tentative plan is real; it just isn't final.
